one_sentence: Fiat currency is structurally equivalent to a thermodynamic conservation violation, where money creation without real backing injects phantom energy that degrades the economic system.
executive_summary: This document establishes a structural isomorphism between the First Law of Thermodynamics (energy conservation) and sound monetary systems (gold standard), arguing that fiat currency violates this conservation principle by creating money without corresponding real output. The mapping shows that fiat printing is analogous to injecting phantom energy without mass, producing waste heat (inflation) and systemic disorder (inequality, debt accumulation). Historical evidence from fiat currency failures (Roman denarius, Continental Dollar, Reichsmark, Zimbabwe dollar) supports the claim that sustained conservation violation leads to terminal states like hyperinflation. The theological layer connects this to biblical prohibitions on false measures and unearned gain, suggesting fiat currency is a structural moral violation. The document acknowledges ontological asymmetry—physics conservation is fundamental, monetary conservation is institutional—but maintains the topology is robust and predictive.
short_summary: This document is an isomorphism record mapping the First Law of Thermodynamics to monetary systems. The core structural claim is that fiat currency violates the conservation principle by creating money without real backing, analogous to injecting phantom energy without mass. Key evidence includes historical fiat currency failures and post-1971 economic data showing inflation and inequality spikes. This matters because it reframes monetary policy as a thermodynamic and moral issue, predicting inevitable degradation of fiat systems.
